assessment: This paper reports fundamental insights into host-transposon interactions, and more specifically how specific genomic loci may be elected for producing anti-transposon piRNAs in Drosophila. The authors provide here compelling evidence that Kipferl, a ZAD zinc-finger protein, helps guide Rhino to G-rich motifs present in piRNA-producing loci in the female germline, demonstrating for the first time the existence of sequence-specific factors in piRNA biogenesis. The findings are of broad interest to the fields of heterochromatin and transposon biology.
